title: Real smoothness and differential of a complex analytic map
statement:
Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $E,F$ be finite-dimensional normed complex vector spaces (each spanned by finitely many vectors), let $U\subseteq E$ be open, and let $f:U\to F$ be complex analytic: near every point it is represented by a convergent complex power series. Then $f$ is $C^\infty$ as a map of real vector spaces. It has a continuous complex-linear differential $D_{\mathbf C}f(x)$ at every $x\in U$. Its real Frechet differential is the same map with scalars restricted to $\mathbf R$:
$$D_{\mathbf R}f(x)[v]=D_{\mathbf C}f(x)[v]\quad(v\in E).$$
